thread:
alex: Hey team — customer AcmeHealth opened an escalation. Their app intermittently gets 502/TLS handshake failures when calling our hosted /v1/generate via their AWS PrivateLink. Only from their prod VPC, ~5-15% of requests fail. They can reproduce with curl.

maria_support: Can you paste a short repro + curl trace and any headers? Also customer account id so we can check endpoint config.

alex: Customer provided trace and dig output. curl shows server cert CN=api.redwood.com (public), but they expect internal cert. Short snippets: 
```
$ dig +short internal-api.acme.internal
dualstack.api.redwood.com.
dualstack-public-alb-123.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com.
52.12.34.56
```
and
```
* Connected to dualstack-public-alb-123... (52.12.34.56)
* TLS 1.2 handshake
* Server certificate: CN=api.redwood.com
* SSL: certificate subject name (api.redwood.com) does not match target host name 'internal-api.acme.internal'
* Received HTTP/1.1 502
```

raj_engineer: That CNAME chain suggests their DNS is resolving our internal hostname to the public ALB, not the interface endpoint ENI IPs. Two likely causes: (A) Private DNS for the interface endpoint not enabled/associated, or (B) they have a VPC resolver/conditional forwarder sending queries to on-prem DNS which returns the public record. Ask them to `dig +trace` against the VPC resolver and against 8.8.8.8 for comparison.

maria_support: I asked for `dig @169.254.169.253 internal-api.acme.internal +short` (their VPC resolver) vs `dig @10.10.10.10 internal-api.acme.internal +short` (their on-prem forwarder). They responded: VPC resolver -> `10.10.50.12` (endpoint ENI), on-prem forwarder -> `dualstack...elb.amazonaws.com`.

megan_oncall: So their outbound resolver rules are prioritizing the on-prem DNS for that zone. When their app sometimes uses the VPC resolver (works) and sometimes the on-prem (broken), you get intermittent failures. Two other things to check: security group egress / corporate firewall egress allowlist — public ALB IP (52.12.34.56) might be allowed while ENI private IPs are not, which would also cause asymmetric failures.

sam_ops: Also confirm whether the interface endpoint was created with "Enable Private DNS" set. If not, private DNS won't override the public CNAME. Run: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc1234 --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].PrivateDnsEnabled'`.

alex: They ran checks: PrivateDnsEnabled=true for the endpoint, but they have an outbound resolver rule that forwards `acme.internal` to on-prem and that server has the public record. Their security firewall only allows TLS to our public IPs and the corporate egress proxy sometimes SNATs to the internet. They also showed occasional traceroutes that go out via NAT and hit the internet.

raj_engineer: Root cause summary (concise): conditional forwarder to on-prem returning public CNAME + egress allowlist/NAT path = intermittent resolution to public ALB -> TLS CN mismatch/502. The fix path: (1) Update resolver rules so queries for internal-api.acme.internal hit the VPC resolver (or remove conditional forwarder for that zone), (2) ensure Route53 private zone (or endpoint private DNS) is associated to the customer's VPC, (3) update egress allowlist / firewall rules to permit the interface endpoint private IP range (or allow DNS through to the VPC resolver), and (4) flush DNS cache on the app hosts.

megan_oncall: Suggested repro commands we provided them to validate quickly: 
```
# force VPC resolver lookup
dig @169.254.169.253 internal-api.acme.internal +short
# force on-prem lookup
dig @10.10.10.10 internal-api.acme.internal +short
# curl directly to endpoint ENI IP to confirm cert/endpoint
curl -v --resolve internal-api.acme.internal:443:10.10.50.12 https://internal-api.acme.internal/v1/generate
# check endpoint config
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc1234 --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].[PrivateDnsEnabled,NetworkInterfaceIds]'
```

infra-bot: Noted: customer vpce-0abc1234 (us-east-1) has PrivateDnsEnabled=true and network interface eni-0f1e2d3c.

sam_ops: They also showed their app hosts were using a local dnsmasq that had cached the public CNAME. Steps to resolve we advised: update resolver rules -> flush dnsmasq and systemd-resolved caches -> update firewall to allow ENI CIDR or remove SNAT for traffic to the endpoint (make endpoint traffic stay in-VPC).

alex: Customer applied changes: removed conditional forwarder for the acme.internal zone, associated Route53 private zone to their VPC, flushed caches, and added firewall rule to permit 10.10.50.0/24 (endpoint ENI CIDR). After fixes they ran 1000 requests and saw 0 failures for 30m.

maria_support: Customer confirmed root cause and accepts the mitigation. They asked for guidance doc — I linked them to our KB: "PrivateLink DNS pitfalls and resolver rule ordering" and recommended tracking resolver rules in infra-as-code.

raj_engineer: Will create an internal postmortem note for knowledge base with repro steps and commands (adding the exact dig/curl snippets).

megan_oncall: Great. Closing on our side — we should add a short public checklist for support: (1) check PrivateDnsEnabled, (2) check VPC resolver vs on-prem forwarder, (3) inspect DNS caches, (4) verify firewall/egress allowlist includes endpoint ENI ranges. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks all — customer happy. Closing the thread. :white_check_mark:
